ranked_facts.why: The presence of basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, as seen in the histological examination, is more characteristic of Pilomatricoma (Calcifying Epithelioma of Malherbe) and not typically found in Epidermal Inclusion Cysts.

The nontender, firm-to-hard nodule inside the tumor is more consistent with Pilomatricoma (Calcifying Epithelioma of Malherbe) or Bullous Pilomatricoma, and less typical of Epidermal Inclusion Cysts or Dermatofibromas.

The presence of basophilic cells and shadow cells in the deep dermis, as seen in the histological examination, is more characteristic of Pilomatricoma (Calcifying Epithelioma of Malherbe) and Bullous Pilomatricoma than Epidermal Inclusion Cyst, which typically does not exhibit these specific cell types.

The gross specimen showing multilocular spaces below the epidermis, a solid tumor in the deep dermis with a chalky-white cut surface, and a lobulated appearance is more indicative of Pilomatricoma (Calcifying Epithelioma of Malherbe) and Bullous Pilomatricoma due to its distinctive calcification and lobular growth pattern, which differs from the typical appearance of an Epidermal Inclusion Cyst.
